voyage.name: Turistik Santiago Hop on – Hop off
voyage.content: A red double-decker bus that passes through the main tourist attractions of the city, including the Central Market, Plaza de Armas, Bellavista, and Parque Metropolitana, among others. Pass is good for the day with departures every half hour during operating hours.

voyage.name: Paso de Uspallata
voyage.price: US$30 per day car rental fee
voyage.content: Rent a car for 1 or 2 days from Santiago and go visit the beautiful Uspallata Pass with Monumento del Cristo Redentor, the Aconcagua Provincial Park for some hiking, the impressive El Puente del Inca or even laid-back Mendoza and its vineyards. The pass road itself is gravel road and a detour from the tunnel which most people use between Chile and Argentina. The views from the pass into Chile and Argentina are breath

voyage.name: Plaza De Armas
voyage.content: The capital's main plaza, also the site of the national cathedral and main post office. It's few blocks from the traditional Central Market and has its own Metro Station. During the last years, Plaza de Armas has been used as a meeting and recreation place for the community of Peruvian immigrants. This has led to lots of cheap international calling centers, traditional Peruvian restaurants and Peruvian spice and food

voyage.name: La Moneda Presidential Palace
voyage.content: Next to the Alameda there is the governmental palace, an Italian neoclassical palace surrounded by more modern buildings with ministries. The squares around them are lined by statues and under one of the squares is an interesting cultural center. Guided one-hour tours are free, but require a reservation of at least seven days in advance (Spanish only).

voyage.name: Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art
voyage.content: The well put-together Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art houses various artefacts from Mesoamerica and South America, featuring cultures such as the Olmec, Maya, and Inca civilizations. Descriptions of the artefacts and the ancients' way of life are well-written in both English and Spanish. Highlights include a Mayan stone stele and Andean mummies, which precede their Egyptian counterparts.

voyage.name: Teatro Municipal
voyage.content: Historical performance venue, including international dance and opera, worth a visit even if just from its outside.

voyage.name: San Francisco Church and Museum
voyage.content: The oldest church in the city. In the plaza, in front of the church, there is a Moaï from Easter Island.

voyage.name: Palacio Cousiño
voyage.price: 4000 pesos. Students with ISIC 3000 pesos. Guided tour only. No pictures inside
voyage.content: 19th century palace owned by a wealthy Spanish-Portuguese family. The architecture is a mix of Spanish and French styles with inspiration taken from the Versailles palace.

voyage.name: Parque Forestal
voyage.content: A long park that runs parallel to the Mapocho River, also site of the National Museum of Fine Arts (Museo de Bellas Artes) and Modern Art Museum. Also known as the green lung of downtown, it's a popular place for cultural and recreational events and activities and the border between the historic center and Barrio Lastarria.

voyage.name: Cerro Santa Lucia
voyage.address: Junction of Santa Lucia and Bernando O'Higgins
voyage.content: A park with fountains and stairs leading up to a fort and viewpoint the top. The summit has a great view of all but the skyscraper-obscured city center. Charles Darwin visited this peak at one point in his travels; his words are immortalized in a plaque at the summit.

voyage.name: Biblioteca Nacional de Chile
voyage.content: The national library was built in the early 20th century near Cerro Santa Lucía. Here you can find archives of all Chilean newspapers and some foreign ones, map and photo archives and an exhibition hall.

voyage.name: Casa Colorada
voyage.content: This colonial building functioned as the seat of the first Chilean leader after independence. It was closed for 14 years due to earthquake damage but has opened once again in 2024. It holds a museum of Santiago's history.

voyage.name: Correo Central
voyage.content: The central post building has a museum of old stamps, letters and mailboxes and even a small replica of the first central post office.

voyage.name: Iglesia San Agustín
voyage.content: The city's second oldest church features beautiful colonial religious artwork, including Cristo de Mayo, a statue of Jesus. The thorn crown fell off during an earthquake and legend has that if someone tries to put the thorn crown back on Christ's head, a new earthquake will strike.

voyage.name: Museo Histórico Nacional de Chile
voyage.content: The national museum showcases both the history and prehistory of today's Chile. There are several temporary themed exhibitions.

voyage.name: Metropolitan Cathedral
voyage.content: One of the city's major landmarks, next to Plaza de Armas.

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
voyage.content: Built to celebrate Chile's 100 year anniversary, this museum boasts 3000 art works from Chile and the rest of Latin America.

voyage.name: La Moneda Cultural Center
voyage.content: Museum located underneath the Presidential Palace, the Cultural Center has rotating art and cultural exhibitions all year. Local crafts and souvenirs are available at middle-high prices in the local gift shop. A café is also within the facilities. Note that most exhibitions are not free of charge, however, prices are very affordable.

voyage.name: Estación Mapocho Cultural Center
voyage.content: Cultural center with theater, dance, music, and other various cultural activities and conferences year-round. Hosts the International Book Fair (Feria Internacional del Libro) every spring.

voyage.name: Centro Cultural Gabriela Mistral (GAM)
voyage.content: An impressive cultural center built on the former military Diego Portales building which was destroyed in a fire. The center has an art and film focused library with free WiFi, a theater, concert halls, a restaurant, a café, and public spaces for resting.

voyage.name: Central Market
voyage.content: As with La Vega, fruit and vegetables are sold, but the attraction here is the fish and seafood brought in fresh daily from the Pacific to be sold under an elaborate wrought-iron roof.

voyage.name: Paseo Ahumada
voyage.content: Paseo Ahumada comprises four blocks between Alameda and Plaza de Armas and is the commercial hub of the city. It features commercial buildings with restaurants, cafés and small and large places to shop.

voyage.name: Dominó
voyage.content: A traditional "soda fountain" that has become a large chain. Known for its rapid service and classic sandwiches and completos.

voyage.name: Donde Guido
voyage.content: Peruvian sandwich place with a large variety of stuffings and sauces to choose from, also many different kinds of fruit smoothies.

voyage.name: El Rápido
voyage.content: Famous for its fast service and fried empanadas of different flavors.

voyage.name: El Naturista
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant with a large variety of products.

voyage.name: Fuente Alemana
voyage.content: One of the most famous sandwich places in the city, the sandwiches are prepared in the front of the customer. Try the churrasco italiano.

voyage.name: Nuria
voyage.content: Founded in 1928 with several restaurants around downtown. They have classic Chilean dishes as well as large sandwiches.

voyage.name: Bar Nacional
voyage.content: Offers hearty Chilean meals and a range of local and imported drinks.

voyage.name: Milano's Pizza
voyage.price: Italian-style pizza that start at 2890 pesos for a personal size and 6450 pesos for a medium. Delivers for 600 pesos

voyage.name: La Joya del Pacífico
voyage.content: Like other eateries in the Mercado central, this restaurant specializes in seafood.

voyage.name: Donde Augusto
voyage.content: One of Mercado Central's largest restaurants, it's famous for traditional Chilean seafood dishes.

voyage.name: La Casona del Centro
voyage.content: Barbecued meat and seafood, and home-made pasta.

voyage.name: Red Pub
voyage.content: Nice bar downtown between lounge bar and more folklorica. Good rock bands often come to play.

voyage.name: Hotel Angamos
voyage.price: 10,000 pesos per double room, includes breakfast
voyage.content: Small hotel with clean and tidy rooms, double beds and hot water on demand. If there is none, you simply ask the owners to turn it on. Family run business and you can turn up to at any time of day/night. Close to the centre and safe. There is no hotel sign, just ring the bell.

voyage.name: casAltura Hostel
voyage.content: Spacious hostel in a beautiful old building with a roof terrace. The interior is modern, comfortable, and always clean. It opened just a few months ago so it can be a little quiet at times, but if you're not looking for a party hostel you're sure to enjoy the laid back atmosphere. Very friendly and helpful staff. Free internet and Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Plaza de Armas Hostel
voyage.price: US$12-16 dormitory, US$34-38 double with shared bathroom, US$48-50 double with private bathroom
voyage.content: On the central square with a great view out over the plaza near the subway and museums. Small (located on an upper floor of a building) but lively place with good staff. Free internet with three computers, Wi-Fi throughout the establishment, common room equipped with a two TVs and a DVD player.

voyage.name: Residencia Tabita
voyage.price: Singles from 8,000 pesos, 15,000 pesos for doubles
voyage.content: Cosy, friendly and quiet, but right in the middle of town. 2,000 pesos for unlimited internet access during your stay using Tabita's computer or Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Casa Moro
voyage.content: A small bed and breakfast with 4 guest rooms; all with private bathrooms, internet access, maid service daily and a great breakfast every morning of your stay. The house is three levels with two patios and many common spaces. Dinner is offered for those who want that option.

voyage.name: Hotel Fundador
voyage.price: Rooms US$145-185 and suites US$205-260 (Apr, Oct - Nov); US$30-50 cheaper at other times
voyage.content: Renovated hotel that is conveniently located for sightseeing in the historic center of the city. It also has a good quality restaurant.

voyage.name: EcoHostel
voyage.content: Nice clean hostel with recycling bins and ecological spirit (though some might find it doutbful, what with the use of a fuel heater, a permanently-on computer, and constant music blaring), away from the hustle and bustle of the city center while still being close enough to walk there. Wi-Fi, hot water, nice kitchen, breakfast included; close to laundry and supermarkets. The noise from the communal area, though not cr

voyage.name: Andes Hostel & Apartments
voyage.content: Mixed and women-only four- to six-bed dorms, private rooms and apartments. Price includes breakfast, Wi-Fi, and daily housekeeping service. Great staff and fun weekly events.

voyage.name: Hostal Santa Lucia
voyage.content: A view of Cerro Santa Lucia located just blocks away from the center. Great personal staff and good breakfast with fresh fruit.

voyage.name: Hostal de la Barra
voyage.content: This hostel is run directly in an old building in the middle of Neighborhood Bellas Artes, it has high quality infrastructure and also has a very nice coffee shop next door where the breakfast is served: The drawback is the six lane road outside which is rarely quiet and the early morning revellers returning home. Sleep is at a premium here. Good points are the staff, the location and the park areas nearby

voyage.name: Caesar Business Santiago Centro
voyage.content: Part of an international chain.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Hotel Santiago
voyage.content: Large hotel near Plaza Italia.

voyage.name: Hotel Panamericano
voyage.content: Located downtown.

voyage.name: Lastarria Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Small luxurious hotel in Barrio Lastarria

voyage.name: Nippon Hotel
voyage.content: Near Plaza Italia.

voyage.name: Torre Telefónica
voyage.content: Until 2010 Santiago's highest building, now surpassed by Torre Titanium La Portada and Gran Torre Santiago.

voyage.name: Plaza Baquedano
voyage.content: The lively little square in the intersection of the two most important avenues of Santiago, Alameda and Vicuña Mackenna is also frequently the place for public meetings such as celebrating sport successes and political demonstrations.

voyage.name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo
voyage.content: Santiago's modern art museum is part of the university's faculty of art. Next to the façade there's a statue by the Colombian artist Fernando Botero.

voyage.name: Gran Torre Santiago
voyage.content: South America's highest building with a viewing platform on the top floor.

voyage.name: Festival de Jazz de Providencia
voyage.content: A very good jazz festival takes place during summer (typically each January) in Providencia. The Festival de Jazz de Providencia takes place each year in Mapocho's riverside and showcasts the best local bands and some international guests. A good budget-conscious alternative for summer nights.

voyage.name: Federación de Andinismo de Chile
voyage.content: The mountaineering foundation founded in 1947 organizes excursions and competitions, as well as offers courses in mountaineering, first aid, and orienteering through its affiliate, the Escuela Nacional de Montaña.

voyage.name: Club Alemán Andino
voyage.content: Founded in 1924, this mountaineering organization offers trekking, bouldering, and climbing excursions and workshops.

voyage.name: Parque Metropolitano de Santiago
voyage.content: One of the city's landmarks, this hill has walking paths, gardens, viewpoints and the Metropolitan zoo.

voyage.name: Parque de las esculturas
voyage.content: A place to relax with many sculptures and good views to the skyline of the financial district.

voyage.name: Mall Costanera Center
voyage.content: The first six floors of the Gran Torre Santiago hold the newest mall in Santiago. A gigantic food court, cinema, supermarket and stores like Banana Republic, H&M, Zara, NTS. Also restaurants and cafes like Crepes&Waffles, Hard Rock Cafe and Applebees.

voyage.name: Mall Vivo Panorámico
voyage.content: Close to Los Leones station, this mall has a bit of everything from ice cream to shoes.

voyage.name: Aquí Está Coco
voyage.content: Seafood is this restaurant's specialty and its menu has a wide variety of fish and shellfish to choose from. There are a number of other dishes for the non-seafood lover as well.

voyage.name: Amadeus
voyage.price: Tasty wood-fired pizzas that start at CLP$3500-4000

voyage.name: Docetrece
voyage.content: A very good place to eat a generous sandwich (try the "Holanda") or a big Chorrillana, and a great variety of national and imported beers.

voyage.name: Baco
voyage.content: A relaxing French restaurant in Providencia, with one of the best wine list of the city.

voyage.name: Hogs
voyage.content: A veritable fast food boutique that sells hot dogs of many different meats and plenty of toppings to choose from.

voyage.name: Vegan Bunker
voyage.content: Phenomenal vegan sandwich place with a feminist flair. English menus available.

voyage.name: El Candil
voyage.content: A quiet bar/restaurant in Providencia. The traffic outside is noticeable but not excessive and drinking outside here has a genuinely pleasant urban flavour. If you fancy making a night of it, Bar Liguria is practically next door.

voyage.name: Bar Liguria
voyage.content: This bar looks like a 1950s American diner and plays music ranging from classic 1950s rock to what you'd hear in a mid-2000s London pub. For all that, it's clearly no tourist trap and the clientele are mainly local. At the weekend the bars on Pio Nono are probably a better bet, but for a mid-week drink this is well worth a visit. It is also a great restaurant during the day. It serves many local dishes and drinks, in

voyage.name: Boomerang
voyage.content: High scale pub and cocktail bar.

voyage.name: Black Rock Pub
voyage.content: An Australian-owned gastropub which offers a wide selection of domestic and international microbrews and cuisine. Watch sports on the multiple TVs inside or enjoy watching the day go by in the tree-shaded terrace. Happy Hour until 22:00 everyday.

voyage.name: Hostal Romandia
voyage.content: Located in a quiet residential district, the Hostal Romandia is a central bed and breakfast style accommodation perfect for business travelers, students, or guests who want to get a good night's sleep in order to discover the fascinating city of Santiago's attractions during their stay.

voyage.name: Atacama Hostel
voyage.content: Hostel is close to bars, restaurants, clubs and both the bus and subway station. Rooms are cozy and colorful, large common room with lots of places to hang out and TV and DVDs, the terrace is a great place for a BBQ and views of the city. The water temperature in the showers here can be a bit temperamental.

voyage.name: Footsteps Backpackers
voyage.content: A nice little hostel not too far from the trendy area of Bellavista.

voyage.name: Castillo Surfista Hostel
voyage.content: Opened by a California surfer in January 2012, this hostel is located a short walk from everything, but the neighborhood is safe and quiet. Private rooms, shared dorms, surfing trips, in-house Spanish classes, and student housing in Santiago are available.

voyage.name: Hostal Providencia
voyage.content: Rooms with private and shared bathrooms in a house with an antique Chilean style with a modern twist. Staff is very helpful. Breakfast, BBQ, common areas with free internet and Wi-Fi, cable TV, books and DVD library. A three minute walk from Metro Baquedano, Plaza Italia and walking distance to Bellavista neighborhood.

voyage.name: Ventana Sur Hostel
voyage.price: US$11-12 dorms, US$21 single with shared bathroom, US$36-44 Double with private bathroom
voyage.content: Chilled out hostel but there's always something going on. Good location with friendly staff who always go the extra mile and are great fun to hang out with. Pool, free internet and WiFi, continental breakfast included, Friday night BBQs, Wednesday free wine nights. Duvets in the dorms.

voyage.name: Furchi E.I.R.L -Furnished Apartments-/ Bilbao3561
voyage.address: Francisco Bilbao & San Juan de Luz
voyage.content: Furnished two-bedroom apartment, 58 m² that sleeps up to four people. Includes full kitchen, washing machine, LCD TV , Cable, Desktop Computer with Internet, WiFi, DVD player, stereo, Chilean Cell Phone and free phone (local, national and international calls). The service also includes local access numbers in many cities around the world to call directly to the apartment as a local call. Other apartments also availab

voyage.name: MG Apartments
voyage.content: Nice views over the city, towel changes must be asked. The apartments have complete kitchens with microwave, oven and hob but no meals or breakfast are provided, although there are many restaurants and cafes like starbucks nearby. Internet access (wi-fi) is included in the price. Furniture are modern and well conserved as are the bed and pillows. There are cable TV and LCD monitors. A good deal and location in the ci

voyage.name: NH Ciudad de Santiago
voyage.content: Elegant hotel in the centre of the city, a short distance from the primary metro line. The hotel contains 122 suites with private bathrooms, and separate bedroom and living room. Rooms contain sofa, minibar, television and Wi-Fi while the hotel itself offers a gym, sauna, and swimming pool.

voyage.name: Meridiano Sur, Petit Hotel
voyage.content: Five double rooms and two singles with private bathroom, satellite TV and Wi-Fi. There is also a loft with room for five.

voyage.name: Café Literario Parque Bustamante
voyage.content: A combination library-café (hence, "literary café") located in the park, free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Café Literario Parque Balmaceda
voyage.content: Similar to the above, except smaller.

voyage.name: Parque Bicentenario
voyage.content: A beautiful park, still under construction. Large extension of grass, children games, dog games, a very nice pond with black neck swans. There is also a restaurant, a café (Le fournil) and Vitacura's city hall. Trails for walking and biking.

voyage.name: Estadio Nacional 'Julio Martínez Prádanos'
voyage.content: This is the site of sports events (both football and others), concerts, and social events including the yearly Teletón charity event. A National Historical Landmark opened in 1938, the World Cup finals were played here in 1962. A decade later, people opposing the dictatorship, were interned here.

voyage.name: Parque Observatorio Cerro Calán
voyage.content: Cerro Calán has been envisioned as an intercommunal park since the early urban development of Las Condes. Originally part of the Hacienda Apoquindo, the area was primarily farmland until the 1950s, when it was divided for urbanization. Known historically as 'Qala' or 'Colón,' meaning "completely bare" in Quechua, the hill was designated for green spaces and later transferred to the University of Chile for the establi

voyage.name: Parque Padre Hurtado
voyage.price: Parking 3500 pesos, using the barbecue equipment 3500 pesos
voyage.content: One of the largest activity parks in Chile, popular among young adults and families on the weekend. Large green expanses, a lake with boats, barbecue grills and there are often unofficial cultural and sports events taking place.

voyage.name: Parque por la Paz Villa Grimaldi
voyage.content: The site of Villa Grimaldi, infamous as a torture center during the Pinochet dictatorship, has now been turned into a memorial park. In 2004 it was listed as a national monument.

voyage.name: Centro Artesanal Los Dominicos
voyage.content: Designed to resemble a traditional Chilean town, its narrow dirt streets and adobe houses with thatched roofs host workshops where artisans create and sell their crafts directly to visitors. The center features cultural events, live performances, and local cuisine. It also houses the Las Condes Wax Museum. Declared a National Monument in 1983, the site preserves the colonial history of the area.

voyage.name: Club de Jazz de Santiago
voyage.content: The Club de Jazz de Santiago is one of the best of the city's many jazz clubs. Located in the northern part of the Ñuñoa neighborhood, this small club routinely brings in some of the best local, national, and international artists specializing in everything from Latin Jazz to Blues to Bossa Nova.

voyage.name: Alto Las Condes
voyage.hours: Stores: daily 10:00-22:00, restaurants until 23:30 (weekday nights) or 00:30 (weekend nights)
voyage.content: Located at the junction of Presidente Kennedy and Padre Hurtado, it's accessible by bus. It's one of the largest malls in Santiago with 5000 parking spaces, 200 stores, medical center, supermarket and movie theater.

voyage.name: Parque Arauco
voyage.hours: Stores: 10:00-21:00, restaurants until 00:00 or 02:00 depending on day
voyage.content: A large mall both by area and sales, accessible by bus. It has large department stores, a medical center, a food court and plenty of restaurants.

voyage.name: Apumanque
voyage.content: At the junction of Avenida Apoquindo and Manquehue Sur, it features chain stores, restaurants and services for kids.

voyage.name: Isidora Goyenechea
voyage.content: A very nice and safe neighbourhood with plenty of high end restaurants.

voyage.name: Temple Asian Lounge
voyage.content: One of the best kept secret in Las Condes, this Japanese restaurant offers incredible dishes, like the Karaage or the Onigiri. Great atmosphere, too.

voyage.name: Boragó
voyage.content: Frequently named as the best restaurant of the country, this innovative place offers "Chilean haute cuisine", using only local and rare ingredients in its dishes.

voyage.name: Anakena
voyage.content: Designed to look like an outdoor market with a number of dishes that combine Asian, European, and South American cooking styles.

voyage.name: Café Dante
voyage.content: A meeting point for friends, with a lot of history and nice service.

voyage.name: La Leyenda
voyage.content: This Peruvian restaurant/bar plays music from all over Latin America at weekends until 05:00 to a diverse crowd of locals with roots all over South America. Unpretentious and entertaining.

voyage.name: Batuta
voyage.content: A good spot to see mainstream Chilean rock and metal bands, although it is expensive by Chilean standards.

voyage.name: Viña Santa Carolina
voyage.content: Founded in 1875, it's now listed as a national monument. Tours are available for 10 persons or above, call them at least three days in advance. The tour goes through houses and cellars and includes wine tasting. The entrance is approximately 600 m from the Rodrigo Araya metro station.

voyage.name: The Ritz-Carlton
voyage.content: A very nice hotel in an orderly and modern neighborhood. There are restaurants and bars nearby, a small park across the street and the neighborhood is modern and organized.

voyage.name: W Santiago
voyage.content: Located in the heart of Santiago's business district, the hotel is very close to South America's tallest skyscraper: the Costanera Center. It has a great bar/restaurant, one spectacular gym and spa (The O2), and plenty of fine restaurants in Isidora Goyenechea street.

voyage.name: Mandarin Oriental, Santiago
voyage.content: Has a 90-m² (1000 sq ft) lagoon-style pool, health club, and several restaurants.

voyage.name: Santiago Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: A popular business hotel in Las Condes, near excellent dining and shopping. Offers comfortable accommodations, a Lobby Bar, two first-rate restaurants, meeting space, and other modern amenities and services.

voyage.name: La Chascona
voyage.content: One of three homes owned by the famous poet Pablo Neruda, La Chascona (meaning tangle-haired woman, after his third wife) is in the artistic Bellavista neighborhood. The house is filled with lots of quirky artifacts collected by Neruda throughout his life, as well as artwork by some of his famous friends. Tours are given in English, French, and Spanish.

voyage.name: Parque Metropolitano
voyage.content: This vast park is home to Cerro San Cristóbal. At 722 ha, it's one of the world's largest urban parks. From the top there is a beautiful view over the city and, on a clear day, the Andes. The summit can be reached by funicular (1500 pesos one way, 2000 pesos return; cheaper for children and seniors, more expensive on weekends and holidays), cable car, or a hike (45-90mins). In the park there is also a Japanese garden

voyage.name: Cementerio General de Santiago
voyage.content: About two million Chileans rest in peace at the country's largest and oldest cemetery, including many important historical figures like Manuel Rodriguez, Violeta Parra, Andres Bello, Maria Luisa Bombal and most presidents of Chile. It's also an open air museum of burial mausoleums in Egyptian, Greek, Gothic, Moorish and almost any other thinkable styles.

voyage.name: Vega central de Santiago
voyage.content: A colorful market with over 500 stalls, selling fruits, vegetables and other food products. The current market building was inaugurated a century ago but farmers have been selling their products at this place since colonial times. Worth visiting for the experience.

voyage.name: Arauco Premium Outlet Buenaventura
voyage.content: It's a little far from Santiago, but there are plenty of stores there. You can find Lacoste, Zara and other trademark stores. You can go there by car, by bus and metro or by taxi. If you are taking the metro, go to the Vespucio norte station at orange line. Then, exit the station and cross the road to catch the bus. The bus number is B05. Make sure that your Bip! card has enough funds for you to come back to the stat

voyage.name: Ciudad Vieja
voyage.content: A great "sanguchería", where you can have some of the most gourmet sandwiches in the city. A place to have a drink with friends at very economical prices.

voyage.name: Galindo
voyage.content: A great place to eat typical Chilean dishes, like "pastel de choclo" or "arrollado huaso", in the middle of Bellavista, typical district of the city nightlife.

voyage.name: Vietnam Discovery
voyage.content: One of the best Vietnamese restaurants in Santiago. Waiters fluent in English.

voyage.name: MosaiCafé
voyage.content: Lots of different types of food, including pizza, seafood, sushi, and sandwiches. Great views from the upper balcony.

voyage.name: The White Rabbit
voyage.content: Intimate and charming restaurant, great for romantic dinners. Wonderful food and very friendly staff. Terrific veggie and non-veggie plates.

voyage.name: Pio Nono
voyage.content: Pio Nono in Bellavista has an intense feeling, bars line the street on either side. The area has a very youthful quality but older visitors shouldn't be intimidated. One of the most lively areas of the city at the weekend.

voyage.name: La Casa Club
voyage.content: Five-level club with each floor catering to different musical tastes, laser show, bar and special events, highly recommended.

voyage.name: Maestra Vida
voyage.content: A place to learn and see performances of salsa and other Latin dances while having a drink.

voyage.name: Dominica Hostel
voyage.content: This restored old house was especially designed to accommodate travelers. Full of common spaces and practically-designed dorm rooms. Located steps away from Cerro San Cristobal.

voyage.name: Hostal del Barrio
voyage.price: 15,000 pesos for a single with own bathroom
voyage.content: Hostel in a quiet area but nonetheless quite near to the hotspots of Barrio Bellavista. The rooms are not huge but very clean, including the bathroom. The German owner cares very much about his clients. Breakfast is included and is rather large for Chilean hostels.

voyage.name: Hostel Bellavista
voyage.content: Hostel in a great area for dining out and nightlife but can be loud on the weekends. The staff is friendly with some glaring exceptions. There are several computers and free Wi-Fi, a large common room equipped with a TV, DVD player, plenty of seating, pool table and a guitar. Very popular with young international backpackers and independent travelers.

voyage.name: La Chimba Hostel
voyage.content: Small budget hostel with friendly staff and great facilities. Near Metro Baquedano, La Chascona, Cerro San Cristobal and the city's best bars and restaurants.

voyage.name: H Rado Hostel
voyage.content: Boutique hostel with cool wall art, a sunny common room, and a huge roof deck. Walking distance to all the great places in Bellavista.

voyage.name: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
voyage.content: One of the city's newest museums showcasing the human rights violations during the Pinochet dictatorship. It has English explanations to some of the showcasing.

voyage.name: Museo Interactivo Mirador
voyage.content: Interactive science and art museum, targeting children. The exhibits can be touched and manipulated by visitors. You can go there by metro, though it's about 1 km away from the closest station Bellavista de la Florida on line 5.

voyage.name: Paseo de la Historieta
voyage.content: In San Miguel, next to Gran Avenida there's a park with statues with figures from Chilean history as they appear in the comic book series Condorito.

voyage.name: Estación Central de Santiago
voyage.content: The country's main railway station, designed by Gustave Eiffel is past its glory days as rail transport has been replaced by planes, buses and cars. Still, this remarkable building is where you will arrive at if you travel to Santiago by train and worth seeing even if you don't. Plus, it has even given the name to the neighborhood it's located in!

voyage.name: Basílica Santuario Nacional de Maipú (Templo Votivo)
voyage.content: Constructed on the orders of Chilean independence leader Bernardo O'Higgins, as he wanted to thank Virgin Mary for the final victory over the Spanish forces in the plains nearby. The best time to visit is the first Sunday after Easter when the Feast of Quasimodo takes place. The basilica complex also includes a museum dedicated to the first Chilean government including documents, clothing, paintings and vehicles.

voyage.name: Parque Quinta Normal
voyage.content: One of the city's largest and most traditional parks, with many museums located in and around it. These include the National Museum of Natural History of Chile, the Museum of Science and Technology, the Railway Museum of Chile. Its surroundings are also the Artequín Museum, the Museum of Memory and Human Rights, the Matucana 100 Cultural Center, and Library of Santiago.

voyage.name: Museo Nacional Aeronáutico y del Espacio
voyage.content: This museum is all about historical Chilean aircraft. It's also a venue for aviation-related events.

voyage.name: Centro Cultural Matucana 100
voyage.content: Inaugurated in 2002, Matucana 100 is an excellent exhibition venue for a variety of arts.

voyage.name: Parque Laguna Carén
voyage.content: A lagoon and wetland area near the highway to Valparaíso. In addition to walking around in you can also practice water activities like fishing or rowing.

voyage.name: Boulevard Lavaud
voyage.price: onion soup 3500 pesos, Coq au vin 7500 pesos, Duck a l'orange 9500 pesos
voyage.content: In Barrio Yungay, Boulevard Lavaud is more than a coffee and restaurant, is part of Santiago history. Better known as La Peluqueria Francesa, is part restaurant, part antique store and part hair salon

voyage.name: Plaza Café
voyage.content: Pleasant place to eat a cheap three-course lunch.

voyage.name: Ocean Pacific
voyage.content: Stylishly blue decorated restaurant that has a broad range of seafood. The take-away parlor next door with the same name, has excellent empanadas.

voyage.name: Santa Isabel
voyage.content: Big supermarket where you can gather the ingredients for your own meal. It also has simple take-away items such as chicken or rice.

voyage.name: Los Buenos Muchachos
voyage.content: Great food and great entertainment.

voyage.name: Ostras Azocar
voyage.content: Nice restaurant to eat Chilean seafood, specially fresh oysters.

voyage.name: Las Delicias de Quirihue
voyage.content: Traditional dishes from rural southern Chile, BBQ, sausages and bean stew are things you can find on the menu.

voyage.name: Las Vacas Gordas
voyage.content: Specializing in BBQ, but they also have many other dishes on the menu.

voyage.name: Viña Santa Rita
voyage.content: The current winery was founded in 1880. Before, this was a ranch, and the place where the Chilean independence leader Bernardo O'Higgins escaped after the defeat against the Spanish at the Battle of Rancagua. Tours need to be booked two days ahead and they include the presentation of the production process, the wine cellars and of course wine tasting.

voyage.name: Casa Bonita Bed&Breakfast
voyage.content: Established in a national monument in a protected historical neighborhood. It offers single and double rooms with or without private bathroom and also has rooms for three or four persons. All rooms have central heating, cable TV and Wi-Fi signal. Rates start from US$58 for a single and US$67 for a double. A varied breakfast, internet access and cable TV are included. This B&B is personally run by its owners, a Dutch-

voyage.name: La Casa Roja
voyage.price: Dorm rooms 7000 pesos. One night free every six nights if paid beforehand
voyage.content: Hostel in an old renovated mansion. The shared kitchen is huge and excellent. It's a party place, so it can get a bit noisy. Run-down area. Pool.

voyage.name: Hostel Cienfuegos
voyage.content: Associate member of Hostelling International.
